name: Cladribine (2-CdA) +/- Rituximab
histology: classic hairy cell leukemia (cHCL); CD11c+, CD25+, CD103+, CD123+, CD19/20/22+, CD5-, CD23-; usually BRAF V600E mutated

biomarkers.note: Classic HCL characteristically harbors the BRAF V600E mutation; variant HCL (vHCL) lacks BRAF V600E and CD25/CD123 and tends to be more aggressive. BRAF status does not gate purine-analog therapy (cladribine is first-line regardless) but distinguishes cHCL from vHCL and later enables BRAF-inhibitor salvage. Per DeVita 12th ed. (lines 281710 to 281725) and Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Hairy Cell Leukemia, v1.2027 (extract line 190, IHC/molecular BRAF V600E testing).

lineOfTherapy: first-line for classic HCL requiring treatment (progressive cytopenias); a preferred initial regimen. May be re-used at relapse if the prior remission was durable (>5 years) per DeVita.

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: indication for treatment present (progressive cytopenias, symptomatic splenomegaly, or systemic symptoms); asymptomatic patients may be observed
active uncontrolled infection should be controlled first; consider low-dose pentostatin before standard-dose purine analog if infection cannot be controlled

drugs.name: Cladribine (2-CdA)
drugs.infusionDuration: continuous IV infusion over 24 hr each day x 7 days

provenance.locator: line 281734 (cladribine 0.1 mg/kg/day as a continuous intravenous infusion for 7 days)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. line 281734. Cladribine 0.1 mg/kg/day as a continuous IV infusion for 7 days, given as a SINGLE course. ALTERNATIVE schedule (source-stated, same total dose): 2-hour IV infusion over 5 days (DeVita line 281735). A weekly schedule is also described in the HCL literature. Cladribine causes prolonged CD4 lymphopenia and immunosuppression; grade 3 to 4 neutropenia occurs in ~65 to 85% of patients with frequent febrile neutropenia (DeVita line 281751). Give PJP (Pneumocystis jirovecii) and herpes/VZV prophylaxis and monitor for opportunistic infection.

drugs.name: Rituximab

provenance.locator: extract lines 132 to 135, 347 to 350 (concurrent rituximab in 8 weekly doses starting Cycle 1 Day 1 with cladribine [CDAR], or 4 weeks after standard 5-day cladribine); dose value 375 mg/m2 weekly x 4 per Harrison 22nd ed. line 385777

drugs.notes: OPTIONAL add-on (Cladribine +/- Rituximab). Concurrent rituximab improves undetectable-MRD complete remission rates (NCCN footnote h, extract lines 132 to 135, 347 to 350): given as 8 weekly doses starting Cycle 1 Day 1 with cladribine (CDAR regimen), OR beginning 4 weeks after a standard 5-day cladribine infusion. Rituximab dose VALUE 375 mg/m2 is sourced to Harrison 22nd ed. line 385777 (375 mg/m2 once a week for 4 weeks); the day here represents the weekly per-dose. Screen hepatitis B before rituximab (reactivation risk).

premedications.name: Rituximab premedication
premedications.notes: acetaminophen and antihistamine per standard rituximab labeling when rituximab is added

supportiveCare: PJP (Pneumocystis jirovecii) prophylaxis and herpes/VZV prophylaxis during and after cladribine (prolonged CD4 lymphopenia).
G-CSF and antimicrobial support for expected grade 3 to 4 neutropenia and febrile neutropenia (DeVita line 281751).
Screen hepatitis B before rituximab if rituximab is added (NCCN HCL diagnostic workup, extract line 211).
Bone marrow response assessment should not be performed before 4 months after cladribine (NCCN footnote, extract line 433).

monitoring: CBC/differential - deep, prolonged neutropenia and lymphopenia
Bone marrow at >= 4 months to assess response (cladribine)

doseModificationRules.text: Control infection first; consider low-dose pentostatin before standard-dose purine analog if infection cannot be controlled (NCCN HCL footnote). Clinical review required.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: line 281734 (cladribine 0.1 mg/kg/day CIV x 7 days; pentostatin 4 mg/m2 q2wk); line 281735 (alternative 2-hr infusion over 5 days); lines 281731 to 281745 (nucleoside analogs are the mainstay of HCL therapy); line 281751 (grade 3 to 4 neutropenia 65 to 85%, febrile neutropenia)

guideline.locator: Cladribine +/- Rituximab as a preferred initial regimen (extract line 288); concurrent rituximab schedule CDAR / delayed (footnote h, extract lines 132 to 135, 347 to 350); cladribine and pentostatin comparable activity (footnote e, extract line 343); infection/low-dose pentostatin caveat (extract line 341); bone marrow response timing >= 4 months (extract line 433); BRAF V600E testing (extract line 190)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for cladribine +/- rituximab, a preferred first-line regimen for classic hairy cell leukemia. The cladribine dose (0.1 mg/kg/day continuous IV infusion for 7 days, single course) is concretely sourced to DeVita 12th ed. line 281734, with the 5-day 2-hour-infusion alternative at line 281735. The optional rituximab add-on schedule (concurrent 8 weekly doses / CDAR, or 4 weeks after cladribine) is sourced to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) HCL v1.2027 footnote h (extract lines 132 to 135, 347 to 350); the rituximab dose value 375 mg/m2 weekly is sourced to Harrison 22nd ed. line 385777. Cladribine immunosuppression with PJP and VZV prophylaxis, and expected prolonged neutropenia/febrile neutropenia, are captured. cycleLengthDays and cycles are set to VERIFY: cladribine is a single course rather than a repeating cycle, and the provided sources do not state a cycle-length/number-of-cycles construct. BRAF V600E note distinguishes classic from variant HCL. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
